question.text: In the context of the Black-Scholes model, N(x) represents:

answer.text: The standard normal cumulative distribution function

explanation.text: The Logic: N(x) is the standard normal CDF — it gives the probability that a normally distributed variable falls below x. It's used in Black-Scholes to calculate the probability-weighted expected payoff. The Trap: N(x) is a mathematical function, not a market term. Cross-Exam Context: Black-Scholes formula components are tested in Series I.
